name: murn
author: physics-agent (invented physics on ASCII pictures)
description: PRIVATE. v2 (hardened after both iteration-1 players cracked v1 in rounds 5-6). Invented gravity on an ASCII scene. Clue is 'GROUND|n': GROUND is the ground row of a picture over '#' (stone), 'o' (wood), '.' (air), 9-16 cells wide; n is how many stones must stand ABOVE the ground (stones lying in the ground row do NOT count -- v1 counted the whole picture). The answer is the whole picture, rows joined by newlines, all rows the same width, LAST row exactly equal to GROUND (spaces read as air, trailing blank lines and ragged right edges tolerated). The law of support: a cell off the ground is held only by the three cells directly beneath it (SW,S,SE). A stone needs EXACTLY two of them occupied; wood needs EXACTLY one; nothing may stand on zero (floating) or on three (over-braced). NEW IN v2: the joints must be staggered -- nothing may rest directly on its own kind, i.e. a stone may not have a stone immediately below it (S) and wood may not have wood immediately below it. Material is otherwise irrelevant for supporting. Consequences: the number of supports fixes the material, and the v1 exploit 'an adjacent pair of stones sustains itself forever, so any quota is free' is dead -- stones now have to be produced by bridging gaps, and the picture zig-zags. Intended discovery path: format and ground-row anchoring from demo 1; the meaning of n needs a demo whose ground row contains stones (the naive 'total stones' reading fails); the support law needs the material-typed window -- counting occupied cells below (the abstraction both v1 players reached) is provably insufficient, since the legality of a cell depends on WHICH material sits directly under it. Measured (2000 clues): the two v1 winning solvers score 0.1%; the v1 rule with the v2 quota scores 2.0%; the v2 rule with the v1 quota scores 1.5%; the correct v2 rule with a one-pass greedy scores 100.0% at ~0.02 ms, so the class stays trivial once cracked. Degenerate witnesses closed: the ground row alone, the empty string, the clue itself, junk, solid pyramids, wood-only towers, recolourings, upside-down answers, off-by-one counts, the ground row repeated k times -- all 0%.
